newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast Lt. crudes fall after ANS cargo sold.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast Lt. crudes fall after ANS cargo sold.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell moderately Friday after a cargo of Alaskan grade sold at a sharply lower discount, traders said.
BP America, a unit of British Petroleum Plc, sold a 400,000 barrel cargo of benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $1.75 under July West Texas/Intermediate (WTI).
Texaco Trading and Marketing bought the June-delivery cargo to run at its Anacortes, Washington, refinery.
The deal increases discounts for ANS by 25 cents a barrel and trimmed outright values to $19.75/19.95 a barrel Friday.

Meanwhile, the market for heavy-gravity California crudes was inactive Friday. Most traders had finished business before today's deadline for space requests on Line 63, the main pipeline between Los Angeles refineries and fields in Bakersfield, Calif.
The last heavy crude deal was Texaco selling at 10 cents under postings mid-week.
Wilmington, an heavy asphalt crude, remained $17.17/17.27/
